subject: anatomy
title: Leg Compartments: Anterior, Lateral, and Superficial Posterior Muscles

steps.tx: The leg is partitioned into three osteofibrous compartments by the tibia, fibula, interosseous membrane, and anterior and posterior intermuscular septa. The **anterior compartment** houses the foot dorsiflexors and toe extensors, receiving sole innervation from the deep peroneal nerve and arterial supply from the anterior tibial artery.
steps.say: The leg is divided into three compartments by the tibia, fibula, and fascial septa. The anterior compartment contains foot dorsiflexors supplied by the deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial artery.

vis.alt: Course and division of common peroneal nerve into deep and superficial branches in the leg
vis.caption: Fascial compartments of the leg and branching pattern of the common peroneal nerve. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The chief muscle of the anterior compartment is the **tibialis anterior**, arising from the upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the tibia. Its robust tendon crosses the front of the ankle beneath the extensor retinacula to insert onto the medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal, executing powerful foot dorsiflexion and inversion.
steps.say: The tibialis anterior arises from the lateral tibia and passes beneath the extensor retinaculum. Inserting onto the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal, it executes foot dorsiflexion and inversion.

left.title: Tibialis Anterior Action
points: Origin: upper two-thirds of lateral tibia
Insertion: medial cuneiform and base of metatarsal 1
Primary dorsiflexor of the ankle joint

right.title: Antagonist: Peroneus Longus
points: Origin: upper two-thirds of lateral fibula
Insertion: medial cuneiform and base of metatarsal 1

steps.tx: The lateral compartment contains two muscles: the peroneus brevis and the **peroneus longus**, both innervated by the superficial peroneal nerve. The tendon of peroneus longus grooves the cuboid bone and traverses obliquely across the sole to insert alongside tibialis anterior, creating a dynamic stirrup supporting the transverse arch.
steps.say: The lateral compartment contains the peroneus longus and brevis, supplied by the superficial peroneal nerve. The peroneus longus tendon crosses the sole to insert beside tibialis anterior, forming a muscular sling for the transverse arch.

rows: Tibialis anterior, EDL, EHL, peroneus tertius

steps.tx: The superficial posterior compartment is dominated by the triceps surae, composed of the gastrocnemius and **soleus** muscles. The gastrocnemius arises by medial and lateral heads from the respective femoral condyles, crossing both the knee and ankle joints to flex the knee and forcefully plantarflex the talocrural joint.
steps.say: The superficial posterior compartment contains the triceps surae, formed by gastrocnemius and soleus. Gastrocnemius originates by two heads from the femoral condyles, crossing two joints to flex the knee and plantarflex the ankle.

left.title: Gastrocnemius Muscle
points: Crosses both knee and ankle joints
Recruited during explosive jumping and sprinting
Weak ankle plantarflexor when knee is flexed

right.title: Soleus Muscle
points: Crosses only the talocrural ankle joint
Slow-twitch type I oxidative fatigue-resistant fibers
Primary antigravity postural stabilizer in standing
Equally effective plantarflexor whether knee is straight or bent

steps.tx: Deep to gastrocnemius lies the broad soleus, arising from the soleal line of the tibia and the posterior fibula. Its proximal attachment forms a tendinous arch beneath which the **popliteal artery** bifurcates into anterior and posterior tibial arteries, and the tibial nerve descends into the deep posterior compartment.
steps.say: Lying deep to gastrocnemius, the soleus arises from the tibia and fibula. Its upper tendinous arch allows the popliteal artery and tibial nerve to enter the deep posterior calf.

nodes.label: Popliteal Artery and Tibial Nerve Exit Fossa Floor
Pass Beneath Fibrous Arch of Soleus Origin
Artery Splits into Anterior and Posterior Tibial Trunks
Enter Deep Posterior Fascial Compartment of Leg

steps.tx: The fleshy bellies of gastrocnemius and soleus unite into the **tendo calcaneus** (Achilles tendon), the thickest and strongest tendon in the human body. Measuring fifteen centimetres in length, it spirals through ninety degrees as it descends to insert into the middle facet of the posterior surface of the calcaneus.
steps.say: Gastrocnemius and soleus merge into the tendo calcaneus, the thickest tendon in the body. Descending fifteen centimeters with a spiral twist, it anchors into the middle facet of the posterior calcaneus.

vis.alt: Plantar and posterior leg neurovascular anatomy, Achilles tendon insertion, and tibial branching
vis.caption: Posterior ankle relationships and distal insertion of the tendo calcaneus. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Violent eccentric loading during push-off can cause complete rupture of the tendo calcaneus, typically occurring in the hypovascular watershed zone two to six centimetres proximal to its calcaneal insertion. Clinical diagnosis is established by the **Simmonds-Thompson test**: squeezing the calf belly fails to elicit passive ankle plantarflexion.
steps.say: Forceful eccentric loading can snap the Achilles tendon in its hypovascular watershed zone above the heel. In the Simmonds-Thompson test, squeezing the calf muscle fails to produce passive plantarflexion.

nodes.label: Audible Pop and Sensation of Being Struck Behind Ankle
Palpable Tendinous Defect 2 to 6 cm Above Calcaneus
Absent Plantarflexion Confirms Complete Tendon Transection

steps.tx: The plantaris is a small vestigial fusiform muscle with a long slender ribbon-like tendon that courses between gastrocnemius and soleus. Often called the **freshman nerve** because inexperienced dissectors mistake its white cord for a nerve, its tendon serves as an autologous tendon graft in reconstructive hand and ankle surgery.
steps.say: The plantaris has a tiny muscle belly and a long ribbon-like tendon coursing between gastrocnemius and soleus. Often termed the freshman nerve by dissection students, it provides donor tissue for reconstructive tendon grafting.

rows: Prone to tennis leg medial head tear
Soleal line of tibia and fibula
